title: Writing: text, lists and callouts
p: A document is made of blocks: paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, callouts and more. This guide covers writing and structuring text and the blocks you will use most, with the shortcuts for the things you do most often.
Quiet.md supports nine heading levels. Two or three are usually enough; deeper levels are useful for long specifications and detailed outlines.
Here are a few examples:
Type one to nine # characters followed by a space. You can also use ⌘ ⌥ 1 through ⌘ ⌥ 9. The slash menu lists the first five levels; ⌘ ⌥ 0 turns a heading back into body text.
Headings appear automatically in the page outline. For a long document, write the outline first and then fill in each section.
Type 1. at the beginning of a heading to enable automatic numbering. Numbers follow the heading hierarchy and update when you insert or move a section.
Start with the problem you want to understand.
Numbering also appears in the outline.
Hover to the left of a heading and click its triangle to hide or show the section below it. Paragraphs and list items with children can fold too.
Folding changes what you see, not what is saved. Click the triangle again to fold this section.
Select some text to reveal the formatting toolbar, or use a shortcut.

img.caption: Select text to reveal the formatting toolbar

p: Styles can overlap: bold and underlined, or italic and crossed out. Markdown formatting is applied when you type the closing marker. Press ⌘ Z once to undo the conversion and keep the literal characters.

callout.p: ~text~, _italic_ and __bold__ need spaces or line boundaries around them. This keeps a name such as file_name from turning into formatting.

p: The toolbar's A control offers text colors and background highlights. Reusing a small set of colors helps readers understand what each one means.
Gray, red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple.
You can combine colors: needs attention or checked and complete. Press ⌘ ⌥ H to apply your last-used colors to another selection. Use the reset option in the color panel to remove them.
To color a whole paragraph, open its block menu and choose a background color. This paragraph uses light blue.
Adjacent paragraphs with the same background visually join into one area.
Select text and press ⌘ K to add a URL, such as the macOS website. With no selection, you can enter both the label and the URL.

ul.li: Typing an address beginning with https://, http:// or www., followed by a space, turns it into a link.
Hover over a link to edit it, remove it or copy its address.
Click a link to open it in your browser.
For links between notes, type @; see Organize and find your notes.

p:
Enter starts a new paragraph. ⇧ Enter inserts a line break inside the current one.
This line belongs to the same paragraph as the one above.
Center text with ⌘ ⇧ E.
Align right with ⌘ ⇧ R.
Restore left alignment with ⌘ ⇧ L. These controls are also in the block menu.

Press Tab to make a paragraph a child of the one above it. Press ⇧ Tab to move it back out.
This is a child paragraph. It moves and folds with its parent.
Children can have children of their own.
h1: Three ways to work with blocks
p: Type / on an empty line. Keep typing to narrow the list, use the arrow keys to choose an item, and press Enter to insert it.

img.caption: Type a slash, search for a block, then press Enter

p: The menu includes text, headings, lists, tasks, code, quotes, callouts, dividers, links, images, files, tables, columns, equations, boards, buttons, reminders and countdowns. Try /table, /code, /callout or /countdown.
Hover to the left of a block to reveal its handle. Click it to open the block menu.

ol.li: Turn into: change a paragraph into a heading, list, task, quote, callout or code block without retyping it.
Indent and align: adjust hierarchy and horizontal alignment.
Color: set the block's text and background colors.
Cut, copy or delete: act on the block and its children.
Add below: insert another block directly underneath.

p: On an empty line, the handle becomes a plus button that opens the insert menu.

Drag the handle to move a block. A blue line marks its destination; dragging to the right can nest it under the previous block. Select several blocks to move them together. You can also press ⌃ ⇧ ↑ or ⌃ ⇧ ↓ to move the current block one place.
Type - or press ⌘ ⇧ 8. Use Tab and ⇧ Tab to change the nesting level.

Type 1. or press ⌘ ⇧ 7. Numbers update automatically, and nested lists use a different numbering style.

p: Type [] or press ⌘ ⌥ T. Click the checkbox, or press ⌘ Enter while the cursor is in the task, to toggle it.
checkbox: Prepare the releaseWrite the notesCapture screenshotsReview the English copy
p: Tasks can be nested, colored and moved, and can live inside tables or callouts.
Type > or press ⌘ ⇧ > to create a quote. Quotes can contain several paragraphs and lists.

ul.li: Prioritize reliability before adding new features.
Review the week's changes every Friday.

p: A callout combines an icon, a background and optional borders. Insert one from the slash menu or transform an existing paragraph.

callout.p: Tip: use a callout for a useful detail readers might otherwise miss.
Complete: the review is done and the next step is clear.
Remember: keep a backup of the notes you care about.
Choose a consistent color for each kind of note.
A quiet, borderless note for supporting details.

p: Hover over a callout to change its text, border and fill colors with the palette control. Click its icon to choose another emoji.
Type --- or press ⌘ ⌥ S. The document theme decides whether the divider is dotted, solid or dashed.
Insert a reminder from the slash menu or press ⌘ ⌥ W. For example, a review could be scheduled for 2026-11-09 10:00, with a year-end deadline of 2026-12-31.

ul.li: Click the date to edit it. Add a time or use an all-day event.
Choose a notification at the event time or in advance. All-day reminders use 9:00 a.m.
Upcoming dates within a week appear orange, overdue dates red, and later dates blue.

callout.p: Quiet.md must be running to send a reminder notification. Quitting the app stops reminders until it is running again.

p: Insert a countdown, then use its pencil control to set a duration or a date. Use the palette to change its color. This example counts down to New Year's Day:
You can enable an in-app notification when the countdown finishes.
A button can open a URL or duplicate the current document. A duplicate button is useful on a reusable meeting or journal template.

p: Hover over a button and edit it to change its label, color or action.

callout.p: Markdown markers such as ## , - and **bold** format as you type, including the full-width ones a Chinese input method produces. The full list is in Markdown in Quiet.md.

ul.li: ⌘ Z undoes an edit; ⌘ ⇧ Z or ⌘ Y redoes it. Continuous typing is grouped into a single undo step.
Copying within Quiet.md preserves styles, colors, tables and images.
Pasting from a web page or Feishu preserves supported document structure. Markdown text is converted on paste.
